Consonantal i

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

throughout preposition and adverb

all over a place, all through a time

also all over, all through

classical

Catull. 101.1: multās per gentēs et multa per aequora vectus
Cato Agr. 37: per hiemem lūcubrātiōne haec facitō

per (+ accusative)

preposition with the accusative

throughout, all over; all through (a time)

All over a space or all through a time: per tōtam domum, all over the house; per hiemem, all through the winter; per tōtam noctem, all night long.

Other words

  • tōtā urbe (ablative alone) — throughout the whole (city, house)

    ablative with tōtus, without a preposition · also used · classical · Ov. Met. 11.609: nūlla domō tōtā est

    A place qualified by tōtus usually stands in the ablative alone (see in).

  • passim — all over, here and there

    adverb · also used · classical · Ov. F. 3.525: passim disjecta per herbās

    Scattered about, in every direction.

Examples

  • multās per gentēs et multa per aequora vectus adveniō

    carried through many peoples and over many seas, I comeCatull. 101.1–2

  • per hiemem lūcubrātiōne haec facitō

    do these jobs through the winter by lamplightCato Agr. 37

  • plēbs venit ac viridēs passim disjecta per herbās pōtat

    the people come and drink, scattered here and there all over the green grassOv. F. 3.525–526

  • nox erat et terrās animālia fessa per omnēs ālituum pecudumque genus sopor altus habēbat

    it was night, and throughout all lands deep sleep held the tired creatures, the birds and the beastsVerg. A. 8.26–27

  • tempora cum causīs Latium dīgesta per annum lāpsaque sub terrās ortaque signa canam

    I shall sing of the seasons set out through the Latin year, and their causes, and the stars that set below the earth and riseOv. F. 1.1–2

See also through, around, in.
